framework: China - GB/T 45654-2025 Cybersecurity Technology: Basic Safety Requirements for Generative AI Services (effective 1 Nov 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Voluntary-type (GB/T) national standard applying to providers; also a reference for regulators and third-party evaluators; supports filing and testing for services with public-opinion or mobilisation capability but does not itself set filing procedures.
what_is_tested: Applicability

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: High-risk systems must comply with the Section 2 requirements taking account of intended purpose and the generally acknowledged state of the art, with the Art. 9 risk management system taken into account.
what_is_tested: Compliance with Arts. 9-15 overall

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: For Annex III points 2 to 8 (critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services, law enforcement, migration, justice/democracy) providers follow the internal-control procedure of Annex VI with no notified body.
what_is_tested: Self-assessment conformity (no third party)

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must notify the Commission within two weeks of meeting (or learning they will meet) the systemic-risk criterion, and may argue exceptionally that their model does not present systemic risks.
what_is_tested: Self-notification of systemic-risk status

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
clause_or_page: Objectives, point A; EC Code page
requirement_paraphrase: The Code is a voluntary tool for demonstrating compliance with Arts. 53 and 55 and states that adherence is not conclusive evidence of compliance; the Commission and AI Board have confirmed it as an adequate voluntary tool.
what_is_tested: Compliance demonstration route for GPAI providers

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Guidance for organisations that develop, produce, deploy or use AI on managing AI-specific risk and integrating risk management into AI activities; published Feb 2023, 26 pages, stage 60.60.
what_is_tested: Risk management process guidance

framework: Japan - AI Basic Plan (Second plan, as of 14 Jul 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Plan calls for proactive evaluation of highly capable frontier AI to deter events threatening national security and for sharing international vulnerability and incident information.
what_is_tested: Frontier AI capability / national security risk evaluation

framework: South Korea - AI Framework Act (AI Basic Act)
requirement_paraphrase: Minister may support voluntary verification and certification; high-impact AI operators should try to obtain certification in advance; public agencies should prefer certified high-impact AI products.
what_is_tested: Voluntary verification/certification
who_tests: Certification scheme (body not specified in text read)

framework: NCA AI Cybersecurity Guidelines (draft, AICG-1:2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends AI-specific penetration testing of AI system components before deployment and periodically afterwards, including testing outputs and system behaviour.
what_is_tested: Exploitable cybersecurity weaknesses in AI components and behaviour

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
clause_or_page: Outcome 7.2 / Process 7.2.1, p.72 (technical testing, generative AI)
requirement_paraphrase: Test for safety and possible harms against individuals or groups using benchmarks and red-teaming, document red-teamer instructions, and have stakeholders judge score acceptability.
what_is_tested: Harm and bias toward groups in generative outputs
who_tests: AI system owner using Project Moonshot

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Policy on Use of AI in the Healthcare Sector (Policy/AI/0.9, 30 Apr 2018)
requirement_paraphrase: AI used in healthcare activities should have graceful-degradation mechanisms with automatic alerts; should be subject to audits and examination by the technology provider; and healthcare end-users must conduct regular audits of AI functionality and report to DoH as needed.
what_is_tested: Fault behaviour (graceful degradation); AI functionality in use
who_tests: Technology provider; owning healthcare entity; DoH

framework: ADGM FSRA Supplementary Guidance - Digital Investment Management
requirement_paraphrase: Managers should protect source code integrity, should be able to modify or stop the model, detect and report programming errors and unexpected outcomes, have contingency plans for failure, and monitor whether the model meets objectives while managing inaccuracy, bias and exceptions risks.
what_is_tested: Model operation: errors, unexpected outcomes, inaccuracy, bias
who_tests: Digital investment manager; board periodically reviews governance

framework: Smart Dubai AI Ethics Principles & Guidelines (Guidelines changelog to v1.11; v1.6 is the Principles changelog)
requirement_paraphrase: Operators should identify the likely impact of incorrect automated decisions, consider internal risk assessments or ethics frameworks, and subject AI systems informing significant decisions to quality checks at least as stringent as those for a human taking the same decision.
what_is_tested: Impact of errors; quality of significant automated decisions

framework: Dubai AI Ethics Toolkit (Digital Dubai consultation page)
requirement_paraphrase: Digital Dubai states the Executive Council advised that the toolkit is to be used by all public entities looking to implement AI systems.
what_is_tested: AI systems of public entities, via the self-assessment toolkit

framework: UAE AI Adoption Guideline in Government Services
requirement_paraphrase: Once the model is ready, it is evaluated against acceptance criteria to confirm readiness for deployment.
what_is_tested: AI/ML model readiness against acceptance criteria before deployment
who_tests: Implementing government entity (not specified in text read)

framework: Federal Decree-Law 45/2021 (PDPL)
requirement_paraphrase: Before processing that uses modern technologies and carries high privacy risk (the Article also names large-scale processing of sensitive data as a trigger), the controller must assess the impact on personal data protection; this includes systematic automated evaluation or profiling with legal or serious effects. The assessment must describe the processing, assess necessity and proportionality, identify risks and propose mitigations.
what_is_tested: Privacy impact of automated processing (incl. profiling)
who_tests: Controller (with Data Protection Officer coordination, Art 21(5))

framework: UK Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS)
clause_or_page: Guidance for public sector bodies (updated 2025-05-08) s.13 Risks, Mitigations and Impact Assessments; updating on substantive changes in s.14
requirement_paraphrase: Record completed impact assessments (e.g. DPIAs; a link suffices), identified risks (data, application, efficacy, outputs, organisational, public engagement) and mitigations; update the record when substantive changes occur such as a pilot moving to production or new training data.
what_is_tested: Disclosure of impact assessments and risks

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Using AI safely and responsibly > Security > Security risks > Using AI > Data and model poisoning
requirement_paraphrase: To counter data and model poisoning, model outputs should be tested against known good responses and systematically tested for bias.
what_is_tested: Output integrity against known-good responses; bias
who_tests: Not specified (passive voice); context refers to the organisation running the model

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
clause_or_page: Appendix A.1.5 Structured Public Feedback, p.49-51
requirement_paraphrase: Describes participatory engagement, field testing and AI red-teaming as structured feedback methods; red-team quality depends on team expertise; diverse, interdisciplinary red teams with domain expertise are suggested; types are general public, expert, combination, and human/AI.
what_is_tested: Red-team composition and method choice
who_tests: Red teams (public, expert, mixed, or AI-assisted)

framework: US OMB Memorandum M-26-04 (11 December 2025) - Increasing Public Trust in AI Through Unbiased AI Principles
clause_or_page: Appendix A s.1(B) Threshold for Enhanced LLM Transparency, items (i)(D), (ii)(A)-(B), (iii)(B), Appendix pp.2-3 of 4
requirement_paraphrase: Depending on planned use, an agency may request more information, such as use of red teaming to continuously assess the model for bias, results and methodology of vendor bias evaluations (e.g. prompt pairs on politically oriented topics), benchmark scores on bias, helpfulness, honesty or accuracy (multi-language where needed), and model evaluation tools for comparing outputs or models.
what_is_tested: Vendor bias evaluations, red-teaming and benchmark results for the LLM
who_tests: LLM vendor/developer conducts evaluations; agency reviews disclosed results
